lines.text: ^@Please start Docker and reinstall keploy if you have applications running on docker
agent             starts keploy agent for hooking and starting proxy
commit-branch     Commit a Keploy branch's pending changes
create-branch     Create a new branch on a Keploy app
create-test-suite Validate a test suite spec from JSON and insert it via api-server
debug             Debug and reproduce Keploy failures locally
diff              compare two keploy test runs and print regressions/fixes
example           Example to record and test via keploy
export            export Keploy tests as postman collection
fix               V1 self-heal classifier for failing API tests (devloop_self_heal entry point)
health            Kubernetes health probe / lifecycle entrypoint
import            import postman collection to Keploy tests
k8s               Connect a Kubernetes cluster to Keploy and record its services
licenses          Print the license Keploy is distributed under, and its third-party notices
list-branches     List branches on a Keploy app
login             Authenticate with your Keploy account
logout            Sign out of your Keploy account
mcp-install       Mint an MCP PAT and install it into the AI agent's config. Pass --editor <name> for a single agent, --all to wire every MCP-aware agent detected on this machine in one shot.
merge-branch      Merge an approved Keploy branch into main
record            record end to end api-calls
report            report the keploy test results from the API calls
sandbox           V1 sandbox commands (local, repo-mode). The cloud-mode sandbox path lives under `keploy record sandbox` and `keploy test sandbox` and is unchanged.
sanitize          sanitize the keploy testcases to remove the sensitive data
skill             Install or list Keploy agent skills
status            Show the Keploy API-test loop state and the recommended next step
test              run the recorded testcases and execute assertions
test-gen          AI agent-based API test generation — run, coverage, init
test-suite-format Print the canonical test-suite step schema
update            update keploy to latest version
update-test-suite Validate edits to a test suite and snapshot-replace it via api-server
upload            Upload local recordings to Keploy
--config-path string      Path to the local directory where keploy configuration file is stored (default ".")

--k8s-proxy-auth          Authenticate through the k8s-proxy instead of the api-server (for CI with no direct api-server/internet access). Defaults on when --k8s-proxy-url (or KEPLOY_K8S_PROXY_URL / keploy.yml cloud.k8sProxyUrl) is set; pass --k8s-proxy-auth=false to opt out. Requires a k8s-proxy URL and KEPLOY_API_KEY.
--manual-login            Use manual login prompt instead of opening browser
--storage-format string   Serialization format for testcases/mocks/reports/mappings: yaml (default) or json (default "yaml")
Use "keploy [command] --help" for more information about a command.
│  ▶ Next step:  keploy login  →  then  keploy mcp-install
│    1. keploy login         — browser OAuth (GitHub / Google / Microsoft).
│                              Unlocks cloud mock storage and dashboard
│    2. keploy mcp-install   — wires Keploy's MCP server into your AI
│       --editor <name>        agent so you can author API tests
│                              commands by hand. The agent detects the
│                              proves they catch bugs via mutation,
│                              captures mocks for sandbox replay, and
│                                keploy mcp-install --all     (every detected agent in one shot)
│                              If you're an AI agent running this, pass
│                              keploy auto-fetches an MCP PAT and writes
│                              it inline into the agent's config — no
│    Then ask your AI agent:  "generate Keploy API tests for this service."
│  ▶ No MCP?  Drive the loop straight from the CLI:
│       keploy status        — shows where you are + the next step (the
│                              "NEXT block"). Re-run it, follow what it
│                              says, repeat. Works in any terminal or AI
│                              agent, no MCP and no setup. The skill that
│                              teaches agents this loop was just installed
